stories.full_text: The morning arrived without ceremony, a pale light pressing through curtains that had not moved in weeks. Something in the air suggested a threshold had been crossed in the night, though nothing visible had changed. The hours passed in that particular way they do when the mind refuses to be still, circling the same worn thought until it loses all meaning. In the end, nothing was resolved—only rearranged, like furniture shifted in a room that no longer felt like home.

The morning arrived without ceremony, a pale light pressing through curtains that had not moved in weeks. Something in the air suggested a threshold had been crossed in the night, though nothing visible had changed. The hours passed in that particular way they do when the mind refuses to be still, circling the same worn thought until it loses all meaning. She left without looking back, and in that small act of restraint, something that had been held for years finally, quietly, released.
